svg.title: From Kratos's adjoint output to a row-ordered array
svg.desc: Kratos reports a gradient as an entity-id keyed dictionary over an adjoint model part; the bridge converts by id into the application's row order so it lines up with every field and can become a training target.

g.text: what Kratos hands out
response.CalculateGradient()
{ 17: [dx, dy, dz],
3: [dx, dy, dz],
keyed by entity id, over the ADJOINT model part -
a separate Model for StructuralMechanics, whose
iteration order need not be the primal's
never convert by iteration order
adjoint_bridge.EvaluateResponse
for each row (node id ascending) look the id up
in the dictionary; missing ids are zero
same row order as graph_bridge, DofFieldMap,
every gather and every exported sample
MakeObjectiveWeights / EvaluateObjective define
the objective once for both adjoints
Kratos's point_temperature AVERAGES over the traced part;
weighted_sum SUMS - a factor that looks like a wrong adjoint
what the application consumes
dJ_dX (N, 3) row k = node ids[k]
AdjointSensitivityProcess writes it to a nodal
variable (SHAPE_SENSITIVITY by default) -
every exporter then carries it unchanged
CreateNpzDataset(output_keys=[...]) makes it a
gradient-carrying training target;
sobolev_training grades the surrogate on it
measured: 4.8x lower gradient error, same model, seed, data

svg.text: Cross-validated: the cantilever's Kratos semi-analytic gradient (a forward difference, which sets the tolerance) agrees with the shipped adjoint to 7e-7,
the diffusion square to 8e-9 with the out-of-plane row exactly zero, and full finite differences through real solves are the third opinion.
SurrogateResponseFunction is the mirror image: a trained model where a response function goes, with autograd or the FEM adjoint as its gradient.
